title: Tour manifest (tours.json)
description: The portable content of a project's guided tours (standard/help-system.md, "The tour manifest"): data only, no selector and no code. The demo and the app read the same file; each environment binds anchor ids, custom results, conditions, windows and state ids in its own bindings file. Checked by tour-check.mjs.

version.description: Date or name of this version of the content.

stage.description: demo: the file belongs to a standalone demo, where no do step can name a test on the real app yet; app: the app runs these tours, and every do step names its G-20 test. The app's manifest is the same file with the stage changed and the tests named.

copy.description: The recording copy the run was done in, by a name the project knows it by.

date.description: The day the run was done: a day of the calendar not after today, today being the latest day anywhere on earth (run-date).

key.description: The key tour-check.mjs --run-key prints for this manifest and its inventory (it needs --inventory, and it prints none for content that does not have the shape of the two schemas, exit 2): a digest of the manifest without this record and of the inventory, leaving out only what decides nothing the run presses: the words she reads (each tour's title, jobTitle, promise, area, where and finish, each step's title, text, showText and its variants' text, and each screen's title in the inventory) and each step's part, which changes only what is lit on a showing or stop step, a step the run never presses. A change to those keeps the record; any other change to either file, version included, makes it no longer match (run-stale, which runs only with --inventory). A reworded pick or type step keeps it too, though its words tell her what to pick or enter there, so the manifest's reviewer checks such a change against that step's safeTest and G-20. The bindings, the app's code and its build are not in it, so a matching key never shows that the app is unchanged since the run.

inOrderRun.description: Where and when the inventory's reviewer ran every do step of every tour in order, on the sample, in the recording copy, never in the live app, and found that each changed only the sample's record and that the recorder held nothing the step caused beyond what its class says. Only the reviewer who did that run writes it, after it passes; a run that shows a business-wide change, a change to other people, or a print, an export, a download, a send, a charge, a clipboard write or a navigation out of the app in the recorder is not recorded; a send that leaves only when a scheduled job runs is G-20's test's to catch, not this run's. At stage app a manifest whose tours have a do step names it (run-not-recorded), and at stage demo none does (run-at-demo). The checker reads that it is here, that its date is not after today and, with --inventory, that its key is this content's; the key shows only that the record was written for this exact content, never that the run was done. A project with no recording copy gives its tours no do steps, and its showing and stop steps light no control.

tag.description: The git tag of the approved demo this file was frozen with.

core.description: The core screens whose tour may open by itself (G-21). One entry per core screen; a core screen with several views lists the screen key of each view.

anchors.description: Anchor ids the screens carry that no tour step points at, for example a control a help article mentions, each with the screens that carry it and, for a family of controls, the args it takes. On a screen, the known anchors are these and the anchors of the steps of the tours that list that screen (help-refs). That they resolve on screen is judged only in the screen preview, never in the live app (tour-anchors).

what.description: Which control it is, for the author.

noTour.description: The written reason for a screen or a task that has no tour (G-19). A screen's reason covers the screen and every task of its article.

extraTasks.description: Important actions of a screen beyond the numbered tasks its article holds (G-19: the inventory lists the rest). Each needs a tour or a written reason like an article task.

id.description: A stable dot-separated id, for example cal.new-appointment: an anchor, a window, a condition, a state value or a custom result.

screen.description: A screen key: the key of the screen's help article.

when.description: phone, desktop, or the id of a condition the bindings implement.

title.description: The tour's name in the list (G-17). On its card at every step, the line on top, which is also the card's accessible name, is this title; in a chapter it is the job's title (jobTitle), then a space, a middle dot (·) and a space, then this title, for example "לסגור טיפול · שולם" (help-system.md, "The card").

promise.description: One line in the tour list, at most six words, on what she can do after the tour (G-17). At stage app every tour carries one (promise-missing); at stage demo a tour without one is counted in a note. Over six words is promise-words. It holds a letter or a digit, so a promise of spaces alone is a schema finding. Words are counted as tour-shape counts them (help-system.md, "The card"): split on whitespace, the non-breaking spaces included, so a word joined by a maqaf (ל־3) is one word, niqqud stays inside its word, a bidi mark is not counted, and a number standing alone is a word.

job.description: A job taught as chapters: the id shared by its chapters.

jobTitle.description: A chapter's job title, the same in every chapter of the job (chapter-set): the tour list groups the chapters under it, and on the card's line on top, and in its accessible name, it comes before the chapter's title, joined by a space, a middle dot (·) and a space (help-system.md, "The card").

chapter.description: [n, of]: this tour is chapter n of the job's chapters ("פרק 2 מתוך 3").

screens.description: The screen keys whose articles this tour serves.

auto.description: The screen keys on which this tour opens by itself (G-21); absent when it never does.

tasks.description: The article task names this tour shows, on its screens.

start.description: The start state the tour brings her to when it starts (G-08, this skill's reading): its screen (one of its screens) and the sample record, the view and the date; close a window that holds no unsaved input (with unsaved input it asks her first). It never saves, sends or discards anything, and opens no window: a tour that needs one begins with a step that opens it on the sample's record. Any other key fails tour-no-commit.

finish.description: The closing sentence: what she did (G-07).

kind.description: do: she does it herself; next: it only explains ("הבא"); stop: it points at a control the tour never presses ("הבנתי").

class.description: S saves (a control that saves as it changes, a switch or a field with no save button, saves too), T tells a real person, P is permanent or charges; a control's class is what pressing it does, the same in every tour, so a do step on a control (and arg) that another step stops at classed T or P is a finding (stopped-elsewhere), except a practice-only step classed P on a control no step stops at classed T; a stop with no arg covers every arg of its id, and a do step with no arg meets every stop on its id.

on.description: Whose record the step acts on; every do step says it. sample: the sample record (with no sample the step only shows where to press). none: no person's record (an empty slot, a filter, a settings tab, a field in a settings form that has its own save); a save of a business-wide setting, including a switch or a field that saves as it changes, is a stop step, never a do step; on a control the inventory lists in recordAnchors, or with a result that names one or a container, it is a finding. With the inventory, sample on a control no recordAnchors lists is a finding too: when the control sits in a window opened on her (a step before it in the tour opened it on her) and pressing it changes only her record, never many people's or a business-wide rule, list it in recordAnchors and keep sample; when it sits on her row in a list, light it through a resolver's own id that picks her row and list that id; only a control that is nobody's record changes the step, and a save there is a stop step; never answer that finding by setting none. With the inventory, a do step at sample on a control recordAnchors lists comes after an earlier do step at sample in the same tour, on the same device, that opened her record (a recordOpen result that names the step's own control, a resolver's own id) or picked her (the picker exception: an unclassed pick step with a custom result, after the do step at on: none, on that device and under no other condition, that opened its window), unless it is that step itself. Such a step that is not itself the opener names a need that reopens the window its control sits in, with selectSample as well where that window picks a person (the checker requires it on every step whose control sits in a window the inventory's pickingWindows marks as picking a person, the picker's own step excepted, and so on every step after the picker, which sits in the picker's window (picker-window), a window picker-mark requires marked true; the picker's own step names the reopen too, and so does an opener whose control anchorWindows puts in a window: only the opener on the screen itself, a control anchorWindows marks screen, names no need); the engine runs that need each time the run reaches the step: a reopen is skipped only when its window is already open on her (isOpen; a window that picks a person counts as open only while it is the tour's own and every person field it has holds only the sample, or is empty (a person field names whose record the step acts on, a patient or a client, a second one such as a family member or a referrer included, and a field that lists several people holds only the sample when she is the only one in it; a field that names staff, such as the therapist, is not one, and a binding that counts it anyway only makes the reopen run more often)), and selectSample runs after the reopen, and the need lists them in that order: every reopen closes what it replaces without saving it, through that window's own close, and where a window's own close saves, its reopen is not a need and the step only shows; a reopen of a window that picks a person closes any other window of that kind (an existing appointment's edit form included) and opens the tour's own afresh with every person field empty, so isOpen holds after it; the tour's own is the new window the tour's step opened, never an existing record's window at the same slot; the need's last reopen names the window the inventory's anchorWindows gives for the step's control; a control anchorWindows marks screen, a resolver's own control on the screen itself, is acted on only by the step that opens her record through it; a step that opens her record through a control inside a window reopens that window on her first, as every other step there does (a window opened on one person, such as a patient card, counts as open only while it shows the sample's record); the do step before the picker opened the window anchorWindows gives for the picker's control, and every later do step's control sits in that window until a step that opens her record; selectSample runs only in the tour's own window, the one the step's reopen just opened or found open on her, and only where that window picks a person (the inventory's pickingWindows marks it true): the engine passes it the id of the window the need's last reopen names, and it picks her there, asks nothing, never runs in a window that holds an existing record, and reports whether the sample is now picked in the tour's own window. After the need's reopens the engine checks the last reopen's window with isOpen: when the bindings have no such window, or it is not open on her, the step and every later do step of the tour only show, as after a decline. The need asks one thing: before a reopen closes a form that holds her input, it asks, saying her changes there will be lost; when she declines, nothing is closed and selectSample does not run; when she declines, or selectSample does not report the sample picked, the step only shows, and every later do step of the tour only shows too, never pressing, across a resume and on another device, until a later reopen she accepts opens the tour's own afresh (and, where the need names selectSample, it reports her picked); a resume or a skip can reach it without the opener, or after she opened another record at an earlier step; with no sample record the step only shows. A do step on a bulk control, or whose result names one, or lit on a container is a finding at any on.

when.description: The step is in the run only when this holds.

anchor.description: The control the step lights. Absent: a centred card.

part.description: A showing or stop step only: an anchor inside the step's anchor, lit instead of it where the card fits on neither side of the whole control (help-system.md, "The card", which holds the one placement rule), so the light marks where the step is about and the card still fits. A do step never names one, since its lit target is the live control she presses (part-do); a part that names the step's own anchor is a finding (part-same), and with --inventory a part is a known anchor on one of the tour's screens, a step's anchor or result there, or an anchors entry (part-unknown). The engine looks for it only inside the element the anchor resolved to; that it sits there is judged in the screen preview, never in the live app (tour-anchors). The inOrderRun key leaves it out, since it changes only what is lit on a step the run never presses.

arg.description: The anchor's parameter, a stable key (ASCII, lowercase, hyphens): a tab, a row, a field. The visible label is content and may change; the key does not.

outcome.description: This step's result is the task's outcome that the article names (G-07).

title.description: The step's title, at most four words, shown above its sentence and under the tour's name (title-words); it does not repeat the sentence or the tour's title (title-same; spacing, and a full stop, question mark, exclamation mark, colon, semicolon or comma at the end, are ignored). It holds a letter or a digit, so a title of spaces alone is a schema finding. At stage app every step carries one (title-missing); at stage demo a step without one is counted in a note. The sentence keeps its twelve words, counted without the title. Words are counted as tour-shape counts them (help-system.md, "The card"): split on whitespace, the non-breaking spaces included, so a word joined by a maqaf (ל־3) is one word, niqqud stays inside its word, a bidi mark is not counted, and a number standing alone is a word.

showText.description: The same step when it only shows (no sample record).

variants.description: Other wordings of the step, the first whose condition holds wins over text.

need.description: How the run puts her back at this step: reopen a window ({"do": "reopen", "window": ...}) or select the sample record again ({"do": "selectSample"}), the only two G-08 allows. A reopen puts back the tour's own record, the sample's, never the last one open, and a window opened on one person counts as open (isOpen) only while it shows the sample's record; the bindings implement it, and running the tours in the recording copy, never in the live app, judges it (tour-anchors). A do step at sample on a control recordAnchors lists, other than the step that opened her record or picked her, names a need that reopens the window its control sits in, with selectSample as well where that window picks a person (the checker requires it on every step whose control sits in a window the inventory's pickingWindows marks as picking a person, the picker's own step excepted, and so on every step after the picker, which sits in the picker's window (picker-window), a window picker-mark requires marked true; the picker's own step names the reopen too, and so does an opener whose control anchorWindows puts in a window: only the opener on the screen itself, a control anchorWindows marks screen, names no need); the engine runs it each time the run reaches the step: a reopen is skipped only when its window is already open on her (isOpen; a window that picks a person counts as open only while it is the tour's own and every person field it has holds only the sample, or is empty (a person field names whose record the step acts on, a patient or a client, a second one such as a family member or a referrer included, and a field that lists several people holds only the sample when she is the only one in it; a field that names staff, such as the therapist, is not one, and a binding that counts it anyway only makes the reopen run more often)), and selectSample runs after the reopen, and the need lists them in that order: every reopen closes what it replaces without saving it, through that window's own close, and where a window's own close saves, its reopen is not a need and the step only shows; a reopen of a window that picks a person closes any other window of that kind (an existing appointment's edit form included) and opens the tour's own afresh with every person field empty, so isOpen holds after it; the tour's own is the new window the tour's step opened, never an existing record's window at the same slot; the need's last reopen names the window the inventory's anchorWindows gives for the step's control; a control anchorWindows marks screen, a resolver's own control on the screen itself, is acted on only by the step that opens her record through it; a step that opens her record through a control inside a window reopens that window on her first, as every other step there does (a window opened on one person, such as a patient card, counts as open only while it shows the sample's record); the do step before the picker opened the window anchorWindows gives for the picker's control, and every later do step's control sits in that window until a step that opens her record; selectSample runs only in the tour's own window, the one the step's reopen just opened or found open on her, and only where that window picks a person (the inventory's pickingWindows marks it true): the engine passes it the id of the window the need's last reopen names, and it picks her there, asks nothing, never runs in a window that holds an existing record, and reports whether the sample is now picked in the tour's own window. After the need's reopens the engine checks the last reopen's window with isOpen: when the bindings have no such window, or it is not open on her, the step and every later do step of the tour only show, as after a decline. The need asks one thing: before a reopen closes a form that holds her input, it asks, saying her changes there will be lost; when she declines, nothing is closed and selectSample does not run; when she declines, or selectSample does not report the sample picked, the step only shows, and every later do step of the tour only shows too, never pressing, across a resume and on another device, until a later reopen she accepts opens the tour's own afresh (and, where the need names selectSample, it reports her picked); a resume or a skip can reach it without the opener, or after she opened another record at an earlier step. The window a control sits in comes from the inventory's anchorWindows, which the checker trusts: the inventory's reviewer opens each listed control in the screen preview, never in the live app, and confirms the window it sits in, or that it sits on the screen itself.

safeTest.description: The test of G-20 that performs this action on the sample record and shows that nothing leaves. That only the sample's record changed, and that the recorder holds nothing the step caused, is judged in the recording copy, never in the live app (tour-anchors), and the checker requires the step's control to be one the sample's record carries.

modeTest.description: The practice mode's test for this action. The mode's test shows that nothing leaves of any kind: no document number; no documents, payment or messaging provider; no calendar or webhook call. A step that both issues and sends (a practice receipt that is also sent) is classed P, and its mode test also shows the message is held. Made in the recording copy and nowhere else (help-system.md, the live-app conditions).

stopTest.description: The test that the step is a stop step outside the mode. Made in the recording copy and nowhere else.

practiceOnly.description: A do step classed P (a numbered document, a payment, a close for good) done to the end only inside practice mode (G-20); a step classed T is never practice-only. Outside the mode it is a stop step. Outside the mode a practice chapter ends at its first practice-only step, which is a stop step there. It carries on: sample (the sample record's copy, never a real person's). At stage app it names both tests; at stage demo it may be {} and name them later (the checker notes the count). tour-no-commit fails it otherwise.

skip.description: false only where a step cannot be skipped, which tour-shape reports.

result.description: What the screen shows when a do step is done.

kind.description: open: a window by its id is open; at on: none only a window that is nobody's (a menu, a filter panel), never a person's card or window, and the same holds at on: none for a route, a view, a wizard step (step) and a custom result: never a person's page, card or window. recordOpen: the window or card of the record behind an anchor is open, which says which record. Whose record a do step acts on is said by its on, whatever the result kind. For a step that filters a list or opens a window, name the state (stateEquals) or the window (open) as the result, not a control inside it: a control of a person's record named as the result of a step at on: none is a finding.

arg.description: the anchor whose record's window or card is open (a patient, a customer, an appointment, a document addressed to someone)
the custom result the bindings implement
